{{AnimePokémonInfobox |type1=Bug |type2=Fighting |trainername=Ash |pokemonname=Heracross |jtrainername=サトシ |jpokemonname=ヘラクロス |tmtrainername=Satoshi |tmpokemonname=Heracros |image=[[File:Ash Heracross.png|250px]] |caption=Ash's Heracross |location={{rt|29|Johto}} |gender=MaleConfirmed via [[List of Pokémon with gender differences|gender differences]]. |epnum=EP119 |epname=A Sappy Ending |prevonum=214 |noevo=incap |current=[[Party|In rotation]] |java1=[[Katsuyuki Konishi]] }} '''Ash's Heracross''' (Japanese: '''サトシのヘラクロス''' ''Satoshi's Heracros'') was the first {{OBP|Pokémon|species}} that {{Ash}} {{pkmn2|caught}} in the [[Johto]] [[region]], and his fifteenth overall. ==In animation== ===History=== ===={{aniseries|GS}}==== [[File:Shingo Scizor Ash Heracross.png|thumb|220px|left|Heracross dodging Blade's attack]] Heracross first appeared in ''[[EP119|A Sappy Ending]]''. One of the Heracross followed {{Ash}} and {{ashfr}} as they tried to figure out a solution to stop a territorial dispute between the Heracross and {{p|Pinsir}}, which, unsurprisingly, came in the form of {{TRT}}. Team Rocket was stopped thanks to the Heracross and the Pinsir were able to return to their forest, leaving the {{p|Butterfree}} and Heracross. However, the same Heracross was still intrigued by Ash and followed him out of the forest. Eventually, Ash saw him following and the Heracross happily allowed himself to be caught. Heracross's battle debut came in ''[[EP120|Roll On, Pokémon!]]'', where he battled one of [[Rochelle]]'s {{p|Donphan}}, easily outclassing it before the battle was interrupted. Although he lost a subsequent battle to her most experienced Donphan, Ash was satisfied that he had gained significant battle experience. He scored a significant victory over [[Nickname|Blade]], [[Shingo]]'s {{p|Scizor}}, in ''[[EP140|Wired for Battle!]]''. He initially had trouble with his {{m|Leer}} attack being ineffective when Blade used {{m|Quick Attack}}. However, Heracross's reaction time of 0.18 gave him the advantage over Scizor's claws, and he soon learned to anticipate Blade's movements. Shingo abandoned his laptop analytics and began to order Blade's battle, where the two proved to be very powerful. However, Heracross managed to dodge Blade's Quick Attack, knocked it off balance when it attempted a {{m|False Swipe}} and finished Blade off with {{m|Horn Attack}}. [[File:Ash Heracross Gary Magmar.png|thumb|220px|Defeating Magmar with Megahorn]] Heracross was sent to {{an|Professor Oak}}'s lab in ''[[EP146|Tricks of the Trade]]'' in exchange for one of [[Ash's Tauros]]. Ash later sent Tauros back in ''[[EP147|The Fire-ing Squad]]'', and left Heracross in the Professor's care so he could study Heracross's behavior further. In ''[[EP160|Air Time!]]'', Heracross appeared at the lab and listened to [[DJ Mary]]'s talk show when she interviewed Ash about his Pokémon and aspirations. Heracross made an appearance in ''[[EP225|Bulbasaur...the Ambassador!]]'' when {{AP|Bulbasaur}} was sent to the lab. He was happy to see Bulbasaur's bulb, drinking the nectar it contained before being smacked away. He soon after helped Bulbasaur break up a fight between the Water and Grass Pokémon. Ash had Heracross return to his team for his [[Silver Conference]] match against [[rival]] {{Gary}}. In ''[[EP269|The Ties That Bind]]'', Ash sent him out to fight Gary's {{p|Nidoqueen}}, but Gary quickly pulled Nidoqueen for his {{p|Magmar}}. Heracross fought Magmar regardless of the [[type]] disadvantage, sending Magmar flying with Fury Attack. Magmar launched a three-pronged attack - {{m|Fire Blast}}, a point-blank {{m|Flamethrower}}, and its own body weight from the fall. However, Heracross overcame the flames by beating them away with his wings. He then broke through Magmar's defense with Megahorn, taking out the Spitfire Pokémon. However, {{TP|Gary|Blastoise}} proved to be a harder challenge, firing a {{m|Hydro Pump}} powerful enough to blow away Heracross's rock cover and take him out of the battle. ====[[Pokémon Chronicles]]==== In ''[[HS04|Showdown at the Oak Corral]]'', Heracross warned the other Pokémon about [[Cassidy]] and [[Butch]]. ===={{aniseries|RS}}==== In ''[[AG133|The Right Place and the Right Mime]]'', Heracross met and shook hands with {{AP|Grovyle}} during Ash's brief return to [[Pallet Town]]. In ''[[AG164|Ka Boom with a View!]]'', Ash used Heracross in the battle against [[Spenser]]. Upon being sent out, Heracross immediately went to eat the sap from Spenser's {{p|Venusaur}}. Heracross managed to knock aside the {{m|Razor Leaf}} with Horn Attack before he was knocked back by a {{m|Vine Whip}}. The two Pokémon rammed into each other with Tackle, both proving to be extremely powerful physically. Heracross struck hard with a Megahorn, then took advantage of the {{m|Solar Beam}} charge-up time to hit again. However, Solar Beam then struck Heracross, knocking him out. ===={{aniseries|DP}}==== [[File:DP183.png|thumb|left|250px|Heracross battling Kicketune]] In ''[[DP138|Strategy Begins at Home!]]'', Ash was reminded of his Heracross when he saw a wild Heracross on a tree. This prompted Ash to tell [[Nathaniel]] about his own Heracross and Heracross's tendency to suck nectar out of Bulbasaur's bulb. In ''[[DP182|An Old Family Blend!]]'', Heracross was intended to be sent to Ash. However, {{AP|Cyndaquil}} was sent instead. He did join Ash for the [[Lily of the Valley Conference]], where he was used for Ash's battle with [[Nando]] in ''[[DP183|League Unleashed!]]''. Heracross was Ash's third and final Pokémon in the match and he was put up against {{TP|Nando|Kricketune}}, and sent flying by {{m|Silver Wind}}. Kricketune then used {{m|Sing}} to put Heracross to sleep. However, while asleep, he was able to dodge Kricketune's {{m|Fury Cutter}} attack because of his newly learned {{m|Sleep Talk}} attack, and combined his other new technique, {{m|Focus Punch}}. After Heracross woke up, he defeated Kricketune with a powerful Megahorn-Horn Attack combo, just before Kricketune attempted another Sing. After the battle, Heracross showed his affection towards Ash by suckling on his head. In ''[[DP189|The Semi-Final Frontier!]]'', Heracross was the first Pokémon to battle {{si|Tobias}} in the semifinals of the [[Lily of the Valley Conference]]. He seemed to be an excellent choice, with a double type advantage over the {{type|Dark}} and a recently learned Hyper Beam, which collided with {{p|Darkrai}}'s {{m|Ice Beam}}. He tried to attack Darkrai with Horn Attack, but was put to sleep by {{m|Dark Void}}. Due to Sleep Talk, he was able to hit the [[Mythical Pokémon]] with a Megahorn, only to be defeated when Darkrai used {{m|Dream Eater}}, which allowed Darkrai to recover some damage dealt by Heracross. {{-}} ===={{aniseries|BW}}==== Heracross was reunited with Ash in ''[[BW142|The Dream Continues!]]'', where he and the rest of Ash's Pokémon posed in a group photo with him. ===={{aniseries|JN}}==== [[File:Ash Johto Pokémon JN132.png|thumb|250px|Heracross encouraging Pikachu in a vision]] In ''[[JN068|Advice to Goh!]]'', Heracross reunited with Ash during his visit to Professor Oak's Laboratory with [[Goh]]. Heracross, along with the rest of Ash's Pokémon at the lab, reunited with Ash in ''[[JN114|Friends, Rivals, Lend Me Your Spirit!]]''. During the visit, he helped train [[Ash's Lucario]] and later watched the battle between Ash and [[Paul]]. Before Ash left, he posed with the rest of Ash's Pokémon in a group photo with him. From ''[[JN118|Battling as Hard as Stone!]]'' onwards, Heracross watched Ash's [[Masters Eight Tournament]] matches against {{an|Steven Stone|Steven}}, {{an|Cynthia}}, and {{an|Leon}}. In ''[[JN132|Partners in Time!]]'', Heracross appeared as a vision to Pikachu during his battle against [[Leon's Charizard]]. After Ash won the battle, Heracross joined the rest of Ash's Pokémon at the lab in celebrating their Trainer's victory. In ''[[JN135|Heroes Unite!]]'', Heracross, along with the rest of the Pokémon at the lab, welcomed Ash back to Pallet Town after his victory over Leon. In ''[[JN143|Ride, Lapras, Ride!]]'', Heracross was shown to have rejoined Ash's team. During the episode, it helped in freeing a trapped {{p|Wailmer}}. Despite Wailmer evolving into a {{p|Wailord}} and getting stuck again, they were able to free the Float Whale Pokémon. In ''[[JN147|The Rainbow and the Pokémon Master!]]'', Heracross assisted Ash in looking for a missing {{p|Charmander}} around Oak's lab, but to no avail. ===Personality and characteristics=== [[File:Ash and Heracross.png|thumb|250px|left|Heracross and Ash]] [[File:Heracross sap.png|thumb|250px|Heracross eating Bulbasaur's sap]] Heracross is an eager but easily distracted Pokémon, especially regarding sap. For example, in ''[[EP131|Fighting Flyer with Fire]]'', {{MTR}} dropped a jar of sap to allow {{TRT}} to escape with {{AP|Pikachu}}. He also likes to suck sap from plants or trees, as well as {{AP|Bulbasaur}}'s bulb whenever the two are together, annoying Bulbasaur enough to use {{m|Vine Whip}} to push him away. Again, this is distracting for him, as in ''[[EP136|Chikorita's Big Upset]]'' when he went for Bulbasaur's bulb before helping to rescue {{AP|Chikorita}}. Heracross doesn't appear to care how much this annoys Bulbasaur. Despite these minor flaws, he is a powerful battler, and also physically strong, capable of throwing {{TRT}}'s tank into the air in ''[[EP142|A Shadow of a Drought]]''. Hercross's strong wings bolster his powerful horn. {{-}} ===Moves used=== {{anmov/h|bug|fighting|Ash Heracross {{#switch: {{#expr: {{#time: U}} mod 5}}|0=Megahorn|1=Sleep Talk|2=Horn Attack|3=Hyper Beam|4=Focus Punch}}.png|Using {{#switch: {{#expr: {{#time: U}} mod 5}}|0=Megahorn|1=Sleep Talk|2=Horn Attack|3=Hyper Beam|4=Focus Punch}}|image2=Ash Heracross {{#switch: {{#expr: {{#time: U}} mod 5}}|0=Tackle|1=Leer|2=Endure|3=Fury Attack|4=Take Down}}.png|caption2=Using {{#switch: {{#expr: {{#time: U}} mod 5}}|0=Tackle|1=Leer|2=Endure|3=Fury Attack|4=Take Down}}}} {{anmov|normal|Tackle|EP120|Roll On, Pokémon!}} {{anmov|normal|Horn Attack|EP120|Roll On, Pokémon!|rec=yes}} {{anmov|normal|Endure|EP120|Roll On, Pokémon!}} {{anmov|normal|Leer|EP140|Wired for Battle!}} {{anmov|normal|Take Down|EP140|Wired for Battle!}} {{anmov|normal|Fury Attack|EP140|Wired for Battle!}} {{anmov|bug|Megahorn|EP269|The Ties That Bind|rec=yes}} {{anmov|normal|Sleep Talk|DP183|League Unleashed!|rec=yes}} {{anmov|fighting|Focus Punch|DP183|League Unleashed!}} {{anmov|normal|Hyper Beam|DP189|The Semi-Final Frontier!|rec=yes}} {{anmov/f|fighting}} * Ash told Heracross to use {{m|Fury Swipes}} in ''[[EP269|The Ties That Bind]]''. ''{{color2|000|S25|Pokémon: To Be a Pokémon Master}}'' |} ==In the manga== [[File:Silver Conference Scoreboard AP.png|thumb|200px|Heracross in [[Ash & Pikachu]]]] ===Ash & Pikachu=== Heracross only appeared on the scoreboard in ''[[SP16|One Half Of A Poké Ball]]''. {{-}} ==Trivia== * Out of the non-temporary {{OBP|Pokémon|species}} that {{Ash}} {{pkmn2|caught}} in [[Johto]], Heracross is the only one to [[List of Pokémon that are not part of an evolutionary line|not be part of an evolutionary line]] and the only one to not appear in a {{pkmn|movie}}. * Heracross is the first of Ash's Pokémon to use a [[multistrike move]]. * Heracross is Ash's first Pokémon to have had a unique [[List of Pokémon with unique type combinations|type combination]]. * Heracross's only {{t|Bug}}- and {{type|Fighting}} [[move]]s, {{m|Megahorn}} and {{m|Focus Punch}}, respectively, are the moves with the highest base [[power]] of their types. * Heracross is the only Pokémon in {{aniseries|PTS}} to have used the moves {{m|Endure}} or {{m|Sleep Talk}}. ==References== ==Related articles== {{Animespecies|Heracross}} {{Ash's Pokémon|bug|fighting}} {{Project Anime notice|no}} [[Category:Ash's Pokémon|Heracross]] [[Category:Male characters (Pokémon)|Heracross]] [[Category:Animated series running gags]] [[Category:Pokémon with animated series move errors]] [[Category:Ash & Pikachu characters]] [[de:Ashs Skaraborn]] [[es:Heracross de Ash]] [[fr:Scarhino de Sacha]] [[it:Heracross di Ash]] [[ja:サトシのヘラクロス]] [[zh:小智的赫拉克罗斯]]
